To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bilirubin is independently and negatively associated with A1C levels in apparently healthy Japanese men and women after adjustment for age, FPG, obesity, inflammation, hemoglobin, and iron.
bilirubin is negatively associated with A1C levels in nondiabetic Japanese adults independently of FPG, age, obesity, inflammation, hemoglobin, and iron.
the A1C level is negatively associated with bilirubin, independent of FPG, age, obesity, inflammation, hemoglobin, and iron, in apparently healthy Japanese men and women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between A1C levels and FPG in healthy subjects.
the effects of iron deficiency on A1C levels in healthy Japanese subjects.
the association of A1C with FPG and other factors related to CVD in apparently healthy Japanese adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bilirubin is a protective antioxidant, which is not only associated with lower CVD and mortality, but also associated with lower A1C levels, independent of FPG, age, obesity, inflammation, hemoglobin, and iron.
bilirubin is negatively associated with risks of all-cause mortality and CVD in nondiabetic and diabetic adults.
the association between A1C and CVD risk in nondiabetic people is not yet fully established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the association of bilirubin and cardiovascular disease is independent of A1C and that the association of A1C with cardiovascular disease is independent from bilirubin.
the relationship between bilirubin and CVD is not straightforward.
bilirubin is a strong independent predictor of cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the A1C is an excellent predictor of future cardiovascular disease, and that it may be better than the fasting glucose.
bilirubin is an important biomarker of health, and that it is a good predictor of mortality.
the A1C test should be used as a screening tool in patients with diabetes.
